full_judgment:
13. The title of the plaint shows that it is a suit for mandatory injunction and the suit was valued at Tk. 300/-. In the prayer portion of the plaint however, there is a prayer, "(a) to pass a decree of mandatory injunction restraining the defendants Nos.1-6 from retaining the suit motor launch in their possession or using or utilizing the same in any manner and returning or retaking the same motor launch to the plaintiff dockyard wherefrom it was forcibly taken on 5.9.83." Para 13 of the plaint is the "Valuation statement: The suit being suit for mandatory injunction which has no market value, the plaintiff puts his own valuation at TK. 300/00 for both jurisdiction and court fees. 

 17. On perusal of the plaint and the written statement of the suit it is found that it is not a suit for simple injunction as provided in Section 7(iv) (d) nor for movable property having no market value as provided in the enumeration under Section 7(iv); it is in substance a suit for recovery of the launch although in first part of the prayer in the plaint, the plaintiff', "wants a decree of mandatory injunction restraining the defendant from retaining the launch ill their possession. Now the question is if the defendant is prohibited from retaining possession thereof what will happen to the launch, where it will remain? Although the first part of the prayer is unclear on this point, the second part is clear enough which says "and returning or retaking the same motor launch to the plaintiff dockyard Thus it is found that although it appears from the cause title to be a "suit for a mandatory injunction" the relief prayed for clearly shows that it is a suit for recovery of the subject-matter of the suit, the motor lunch which has a market value.
